questions.question: Examine the relationship between moisture content and spice trading. Which interpretation is most appropriate? a). Moisture can affect both product stability and the weight used for pricing b). Moisture has no effect on traded weight once the spice is graded c). Higher moisture always indicates better spice quality d). Moisture determination is mainly used to estimate volatile-oil composition / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Saffron
  • Active constituents: Crocin, picrocrocin and safranal.
  • Dietary uses:
  • • Used in rice dishes, desserts, sweets and confectionery.
  • • Added to milk-based preparations and beverages.
  • • Crocin provides golden-yellow colour, picrocrocin contributes bitterness, and safranal
  • contributes characteristic aroma.
  • Medicinal significance:
  • • Contains antioxidant compounds, particularly crocin.
  • • Has been studied for potential effects on mood and other aspects of health.
  • • Traditionally used in certain preparations to support general well-being.
  • Cinnamon, clove, fennel, fenugreek, nutmeg, mace and saffron have important dietary applications
  • because of their characteristic flavour, aroma and colour. Their bioactive constituents also contribute
  • to their traditional medicinal uses and are subjects of scientific research. However, these spices should
  • not replace prescribed medicines or established medical treatments.

  • non-volatile constituents in determining the characteristic properties of oleoresins. [U] / [CO4]
  • Definition
  • Oleoresins are concentrated, semi-solid or viscous extracts obtained from spices and aromatic plant
  • materials, generally by solvent extraction. They contain both volatile essential oils and non-volatile
  • resinous constituents, providing the characteristic aroma, flavour, colour and pungency of the original
  • spice.
  • Chemical composition of oleoresins
  • Oleoresins are complex mixtures of volatile and non-volatile organic compounds.
